newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Aristocrat says shuffle hit U.S. plans.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Aristocrat says shuffle hit U.S. plans.

text.p: Gaming machine maker Aristocrat Leisure Ltd said on Tuesday last year's boardroom shuffle had temporarily set back the group's plans for gaming licences in the key U.S. state of Nevada.
"There is no doubt that the boardroom chnages of last year set back our licence application in Nevada," managing director John Dougall told reporters at a company luncheon.

In November, Dougall was appointed executive chairman and managing director in a surprise move. Earlier on Teusday, Aristocrat reappointed Frank Burke to the board after he was dumped at the last annual meeting.
Burke was dumped from the board along Geoff Ainsworth, a member of the Ainsworth family who control about 58 percent of Aristocrat.
The gaming machine maker plans to lift the number of directors on the board to eight from seven now.
Dougall said Aristocrat plans to appoint a non-executive director next month, who will also become the company chairman.
Dougall plans to step down from the chairmanship and retain the position of managing director.
Aristocrat has previously said access to the Nevada market was of great importance to the future growth of the group.
Investors wiped almost a quarter off Aristocrat's market capitalisation following the boardroom shuffle in November.
Aristocrat shares hit A$3.05 on December 5, down from a record of A$4.00 on November 15.
Dougall said the selling was mostly from U.S. pension funds, which control about 20 percent of the stock.
At 2.45 p.m. (0345 GMT), Aristocrat shares were two cents lower at A$3.28.
